text:
Maria: quick q — if automatic fallback triggers (e.g., request timeout -> degrade) does usage still count against customer quota? billing reports are unclear.
Tyler: generally we mark the request as "served" by the fallback path, so tokens are counted. we could change semantics but it's a product decision.
Sasha: heads-up: increasing telemetry for fallback events will add cost + noise. recommend we only ramp sampling for a short window during anomalies or canary windows.
Anika: UX thought: show a compact "fallback rate" chip on the rollout card and a link to sampled traces. let operators toggle sample intensity (off / low / high) per rollout.
Ryan: we also need a stable decision_trace field on inference events: primary | fallback | quarantine and a reason enum. minimal example: 
```
{"decision_trace": {"mode":"fallback","reason":"timeout","policy_id":"rollout-7"}}
```
Tyler: +1 for decision_trace. important: scrub PII and model outputs. traces should be off by default and only sampled. avoid expanding per-request payload unless sampling is enabled.
Maria: billing implications — if we mark fallback requests as not billable during canary, ops will love it but customers could exploit it by flipping rollouts repeatedly.
Anika: compromise: introduce a "grace budget" per rollout: first N tokens free in X time window. show remaining budget in the rollout UI and in invoice exports.
Sasha: telemetry sampling policy suggestion: when fallback_rate(route) > threshold, bump sampling to high for that route for T minutes; apply exponential backoff decay after.
Tyler: implementation notes: router already emits fallback counters. we can add a gateway-level cheap counter and a sampling-config push to trace-ingest. pseudocode:
```
// pseudocode
if (fallback_count(route, 60s) > 5) set_sampler(route, "high", 900s)
```
Ryan: do we want fallback decisions written to customer audit logs? security might request that for compliance.
Maria: yes, but audit logs should include only metadata (decision mode, policy id, reason code, operator overrides). redact model outputs.
Anika: UX mock: add an "operator override" action on rollout page that pauses fallback routing. pressing it requires a short justification and creates an audit event.
Sasha: overrides need rate limiting and role checks so they can't be abused. tie to SSO groups and require justification when outside normal hours.
Tyler: also ensure fallback metrics are taggable by billing project/org so Finance can run reports per-customer.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: noted — ops playbook item created: "fallback-escalation + sampling-trigger config" pushed to staging.
Maria: next steps: Tyler to spec API fields + backwards-compat migration notes; Anika to produce mockups with the grace budget UI; Sasha to propose sampling decay curves + cost estimate; Ryan to draft audit schema. sync Fri 10am.
Tyler: will open a PR for the API proto and router changes, including a feature flag for sampling.
Anika: will post Figma link in this channel when ready :eyes:.
Sasha: quick cost note: if fallback sampling goes to high for ~1% of routes, rough incremental cost ~$3k/mo (need exact numbers).
Maria: thanks all. anyone object to moving forward with that plan?
Tyler: no objections from eng-platform.
Ryan: 👍
